## Today {.unnumbered}

Today you build **Milestone M1**. Reading: **Moraga Ch. 12**.

> **M1 --- Static dashboard** A `flexdashboard`
> that loads your data and displays at least one map and one time series,
> deployed or renderable from your repository.

Nothing in M1 is new. You have made `leaflet` maps since Exercise 4 and
`ggplot2` charts since the first week. A dashboard only puts them **side by
side on one screen**. We build one together on lung cancer in Ohio, then you
swap in your own data.

| M1 asks for | Where it is today |
|---|---|
| a `flexdashboard` | §2, one file and three symbols |
| loads your data | §3.1 and §4 |
| at least one map | §3.2 |
| at least one time series | §3.3 |
| renderable from your repository | §3.6 |
| deployed (optional) | §3.7 |

Install the three new packages once, in the **Console**:

```{r}
#| label: install
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: false

install.packages(c("flexdashboard", "plotly", "DT"))
```

# What a dashboard is

A report scrolls: you read it top to bottom, once. A dashboard fits **one
screen**, and each panel answers one question about the same data. In ours,
the map answers *where*, the time series *when*, and the table *which county,
exactly*. The reader looks at all three at once.

# One file, three symbols

A `flexdashboard` is an R Markdown file (`.Rmd`) with one line in its YAML
header. The layout is written with three symbols:

| You type | You get |
|---|---|
| `output: flexdashboard::flex_dashboard` | a dashboard instead of a report |
| `Column {data-width=600}`, then a line of dashes `-----` | a new column; widths are relative |
| `### Title` | a panel, with its title |
| an R chunk under `###` | what the panel shows |
| `> text` under the chunk | a small note at the bottom of the panel |

This skeleton:

````markdown
---
title: "Lung cancer in Ohio, 1968--1988"
output: flexdashboard::flex_dashboard
---

`r ''````{r setup, include=FALSE}
# packages and data: runs once, shows nothing
```

Column {data-width=600}
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

### Map

Column {data-width=400}
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

### Time series

### Table
````

gives this screen:

```{=html}
<div style="max-width:640px;margin:1em auto;font-family:SFMono-Regular,Menlo,Consolas,monospace;font-size:0.85em;">
  <div style="background:#2780e3;color:#fff;padding:6px 10px;border-radius:6px 6px 0 0;">title: Lung cancer in Ohio, 1968&ndash;1988</div>
  <div style="display:grid;grid-template-columns:3fr 2fr;grid-template-rows:110px 110px;gap:8px;padding:8px;background:#f2f2f2;border-radius:0 0 6px 6px;">
    <div style="grid-row:1 / 3;background:#fff;border:1px solid #ccc;border-radius:4px;padding:8px;">### Map<br><span style="color:#888;">Column {data-width=600}</span></div>
    <div style="background:#fff;border:1px solid #ccc;border-radius:4px;padding:8px;">### Time series<br><span style="color:#888;">Column {data-width=400}</span></div>
    <div style="background:#fff;border:1px solid #ccc;border-radius:4px;padding:8px;">### Table</div>
  </div>
</div>
```

Two columns; the second holds two panels stacked. This is exactly Moraga's
PM~2.5~ dashboard (Ch. 12), with a time series in place of the histogram.

::: {.callout-note}
## Why `.Rmd` and not `.qmd`?
`flexdashboard` is an R Markdown format, and Moraga Ch. 12--15 build on it.
For M2 we add Shiny to this same file with one line in the YAML header. So the
dashboard is the one `.Rmd` file in your repository; everything else stays
`.qmd`.
:::

# Worked example: lung cancer in Ohio

The data of Moraga Ch. 7: lung cancer cases in the 88 counties of Ohio, every
year from 1968 to 1988. One row per county and year:

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `GEOID` | county FIPS code, to join with the boundaries |
| `county` | county name |
| `year` | 1968, ..., 1988 |
| `Y` | observed cases |
| `E` | expected cases (indirect standardization, by age and sex) |
| `population` | population at risk |

Save the CSV in your `data/` folder, as in Exercises 4--7.

## Load and summarise the data

This chunk goes at the top of the dashboard, before the first column. It runs
once and shows nothing; every panel can use what it creates.

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| code-fold: false

library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(ggplot2)
library(plotly)
library(leaflet)
library(DT)
library(tigris)
options(tigris_use_cache = TRUE)

# data: one row per county and year
oh <- read_csv("data/ohio_lung_cancer_1968_1988.csv",
               col_types = cols(GEOID = "c"))          # GEOID as text

# boundaries
oh_map <- counties(state = "OH", cb = TRUE, year = 2020,
                   progress_bar = FALSE) |>
  st_transform(4326)                             # leaflet wants lon/lat

# for the map: one row per county
by_county <- oh |>
  group_by(GEOID) |>
  summarise(Y = sum(Y), E = sum(E), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(SIR = Y / E)

oh_map <- left_join(oh_map, by_county, by = "GEOID")

# for the time series: one row per year
focus <- "Cuyahoga"                              # county to follow

by_year <- bind_rows(
  oh |> group_by(year) |>
    summarise(Y = sum(Y), E = sum(E), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(area = "Ohio"),
  oh |> filter(county == focus) |>
    mutate(area = focus)
) |>
  mutate(SIR = Y / E)
```

The same data, **summarised twice**: over the years for the map
(`by_county`, `r nrow(by_county)` rows), and over the counties for the time
series (`by_year`, one row per year for Ohio and one per year for
`r focus` County). That is the whole idea of M1.

Check the join before going further: the number of counties without data
should be zero.

```{r}
#| label: check-join
#| code-fold: false

sum(is.na(oh_map$SIR))                                 # should be 0
```

## The map

The leaflet map of Exercise 4: the SIR, with the same classes and the same
red--blue colours, so that the neutral class sits around 1.

```{r}
#| label: map
#| code-fold: false

breaks <- c(0, 0.5, 2/3, 0.9, 1/0.9, 1.5, 2, Inf)  # Exercise 4 classes
pal <- colorBin(rev(RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(7, "RdBu")),
                domain = oh_map$SIR, bins = breaks)

leaflet(oh_map) |>
  addTiles() |>
  addPolygons(
    fillColor = ~pal(SIR), fillOpacity = 0.8,
    color = "white", weight = 1,
    label = ~sprintf("%s: SIR %.2f (%.0f observed, %.0f expected)",
                     NAME, SIR, Y, E),
    highlightOptions = highlightOptions(weight = 2, color = "black",
                                        bringToFront = TRUE)
  ) |>
  addLegend("bottomright", pal = pal, values = ~SIR, title = "SIR",
            labFormat = labelFormat(digits = 2), opacity = 0.8)
```

Hover over a county: the label gives its observed and expected cases, so the
reader can judge whether a dark colour rests on many cases or on a handful.

## The time series

An ordinary `ggplot`: one line for Ohio, one for `r focus` County, and a
dashed line at 1, as many cases as expected.

```{r}
#| label: ts-static
#| code-fold: false

cols <- setNames(c("black", "#B2182B"), c("Ohio", focus))

p <- ggplot(by_year, aes(year, SIR, colour = area)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = 2, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 1.2) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = cols) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "SIR", colour = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()

p
```

One more line makes it interactive: hover for the values, drag to zoom,
double-click to reset.

```{r}
#| label: ts-plotly
#| code-fold: false

ggplotly(p)                                  # hover, zoom
```

Ohio's SIR rose from `r sprintf("%.2f", by_year$SIR[by_year$area == "Ohio"][1])`
in 1968 to `r sprintf("%.2f", tail(by_year$SIR[by_year$area == "Ohio"], 1))` in
1988. The expected cases use one set of rates for the whole period, so the
map averages over this rise; in M2 the reader will pick the year.

## The table (optional)

Not required for M1, but it costs four lines and gives the exact numbers
behind the colours. Click a column header to sort.

```{r}
#| label: table
#| code-fold: false

oh_map |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  transmute(County = NAME, Observed = Y,
            Expected = round(E, 1), SIR = round(SIR, 2)) |>
  arrange(desc(SIR)) |>
  datatable(rownames = FALSE, options = list(pageLength = 10))
```

## Put it together

Paste the chunks of §3.1--§3.4 under their `###` panels. Two additions to the
YAML header: `theme: cosmo`, the look of our course pages, and
`source_code: embed`, a **Source Code** button in the corner, so that I can
read your code from the dashboard itself. The whole file:

````markdown
---
title: "Lung cancer in Ohio, 1968--1988"
output:
  flexdashboard::flex_dashboard:
    orientation: columns
    vertical_layout: fill
    theme: cosmo
    source_code: embed
---

`r ''````{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(flexdashboard)
library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(ggplot2)
library(plotly)
library(leaflet)
library(DT)
library(tigris)
options(tigris_use_cache = TRUE)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)

# data: one row per county and year
oh <- read_csv("data/ohio_lung_cancer_1968_1988.csv",
               col_types = cols(GEOID = "c"))          # GEOID as text

# boundaries
oh_map <- counties(state = "OH", cb = TRUE, year = 2020,
                   progress_bar = FALSE) |>
  st_transform(4326)                             # leaflet wants lon/lat

# for the map: one row per county
by_county <- oh |>
  group_by(GEOID) |>
  summarise(Y = sum(Y), E = sum(E), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(SIR = Y / E)

oh_map <- left_join(oh_map, by_county, by = "GEOID")

# for the time series: one row per year
focus <- "Cuyahoga"                              # county to follow

by_year <- bind_rows(
  oh |> group_by(year) |>
    summarise(Y = sum(Y), E = sum(E), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(area = "Ohio"),
  oh |> filter(county == focus) |>
    mutate(area = focus)
) |>
  mutate(SIR = Y / E)
```

Column {data-width=600}
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

### Standardized incidence ratio (SIR) by county, 1968--1988

`r ''````{r map}
breaks <- c(0, 0.5, 2/3, 0.9, 1/0.9, 1.5, 2, Inf)  # Exercise 4 classes
pal <- colorBin(rev(RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(7, "RdBu")),
                domain = oh_map$SIR, bins = breaks)

leaflet(oh_map) |>
  addProviderTiles("CartoDB.Positron") |>
  addPolygons(
    fillColor = ~pal(SIR), fillOpacity = 0.8,
    color = "white", weight = 1,
    label = ~sprintf("%s: SIR %.2f (%.0f observed, %.0f expected)",
                     NAME, SIR, Y, E),
    highlightOptions = highlightOptions(weight = 2, color = "black",
                                        bringToFront = TRUE)
  ) |>
  addLegend("bottomright", pal = pal, values = ~SIR, title = "SIR",
            labFormat = labelFormat(digits = 2), opacity = 0.8)
```

> SIR = observed / expected. Red: more cases than expected; blue: fewer.

Column {data-width=400}
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

### SIR by year (dashed line: as many cases as expected)

`r ''````{r timeseries}
cols <- setNames(c("black", "#B2182B"), c("Ohio", focus))

p <- ggplot(by_year, aes(year, SIR, colour = area)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = 2, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 1.2) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = cols) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "SIR", colour = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()

ggplotly(p)                                  # hover, zoom
```

### Counties

`r ''````{r table}
oh_map |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  transmute(County = NAME, Observed = Y,
            Expected = round(E, 1), SIR = round(SIR, 2)) |>
  arrange(desc(SIR)) |>
  datatable(rownames = FALSE, options = list(pageLength = 10))
```

> Data: Moraga (2019), Ch. 7. Boundaries: US Census Bureau, via `tigris`.
````

## Render it

Save the file as **`dashboard.Rmd`** at the top of your repository, next to
the `data/` folder, and click **Knit** in RStudio (or run
`rmarkdown::render("dashboard.Rmd")` in the Console). You get
`dashboard.html`: one self-contained file that opens in any browser.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Knit, not `quarto render`
Quarto does not know the `flexdashboard` format. Rendered with Quarto, the
file comes out as an ordinary scrolling page, with the panel titles as
headings. If your "dashboard" scrolls like a report, this is why.
:::

That is M1: **renderable from your repository**.

## Put it online (optional for M1)

Your exercises are a Quarto website published from `docs/`. Two entries in
`_quarto.yml` add the dashboard to it:

```yaml
project:
  type: website
  output-dir: docs
  render:
    - "*.qmd"          # Quarto renders the .qmd pages only
  resources:
    - dashboard.html   # and copies the knitted dashboard into docs/
```

Then, each time: **Knit** `dashboard.Rmd`, run `quarto render`, and commit
and push with GitHub Desktop. The dashboard is at
`https://<username>.github.io/<repository>/dashboard.html`. Add a link to it
from `index.qmd`:

```markdown
[My dashboard](dashboard.html)
```

# Your turn: from Ohio to your data

Copy `dashboard.Rmd`, keep the layout, and change only the setup chunk:

| In the example | For your data |
|---|---|
| `read_csv("data/ohio_lung_cancer_1968_1988.csv", ...)` | your file, in `data/` |
| `col_types = cols(GEOID = "c")` | your ID column, as text; pad lost zeros with `sprintf("%05d", ...)` as in Exercise 4 |
| `counties(state = "OH", ...)` | your state; `tracts()` or `zctas()` for other units |
| `Y`, `E` | your observed and expected counts |
| `year` | your time column; months or weeks work as a `Date` |
| `focus <- "Cuyahoga"` | one area of your data |

::: {.callout-tip}
## No expected counts?
Map a rate instead, with a sequential palette, since a rate has no neutral
value:

```{r}
#| label: rate
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: false

by_county <- mutate(by_county, rate = 1e5 * cases / population)   # per 100,000
pal <- colorQuantile("YlOrRd", by_county$rate, n = 5)              # quintiles
# then, in addPolygons(): fillColor = ~pal(rate)
```

Point data (case or facility locations): `addCircleMarkers()` in place of
`addPolygons()`, with a time series of counts per period.
:::

# Before you demonstrate M1

1. **Session > Restart R**, then **Knit**: it renders from a clean start.
2. The data are read with a relative path, `data/...`, never `C:/Users/...`.
3. The map has a legend, and its title says what, where and when.
4. The time series has a labelled axis, with units.
5. A `>` note under a panel names the data source.

# When it breaks

| What you see | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| A scrolling page, not a dashboard | rendered with `quarto render`, or saved as `.qmd` | save as `.Rmd`, click **Knit** |
| `object 'oh' not found` in a panel | data loaded below the first `Column` | setup chunk first, before any `Column` |
| A grey map | the join failed: all SIRs are `NA` | `GEOID` as text; `sum(is.na(oh_map$SIR))` |
| Warning: *not long-lat data* | no `st_transform(4326)` | add it after `counties()` |
| `there is no package called 'flexdashboard'` | not installed | `install.packages(c("flexdashboard", "plotly", "DT"))` |
| Squashed panels | too many panels in one column | fewer panels, or `vertical_layout: scroll` |
| Knits, but not on GitHub Pages | `dashboard.html` not copied to `docs/` | check `resources:`, rerun `quarto render`, push |

If Knit fails on your laptop, use a lab machine or
[Posit Cloud](https://posit.cloud): renderable from your repository is
enough for M1.
